full_judgment: 6. On consideration of the evidence adduced by the parties the trial Court held that the Will (marked Ext. 1) executed and registered by Hara Nathk Sarkat in favour of the plaintiff was genuine and he acquired title on the basis of the said Will to the suit property. The trial court, however, found that Akbar Ali, father of the contesting defendant, had purchased 1.75 acres out of the suit property from Manik by kabala Ext. A (1) dated 31.5.52, that Nagendra Nath transferred 0.29 acre of suit Khatian No. 198 to the said Akbar Ali by registered kabala Ext. A (2) dated 23.5.57 and that Manik and Nagen having been in possession after the death of their father Hara Nath Sarkar and thereafter the contesting defendant being in possession of the said transferred land in denial of the plaintiffs title for more than 12 Years the title of the plaintiff in respect of the same had extinguished by adverse possession. The trial Court also found from Ext. A that Nagendra Nath had transferred some property to one Majibur Rahman who was in possession of the same and this Majibur Rahman having not been made a party to the suit, the suit suffered from defect of party. Similarly one Suren Sarkar, son of Hara Mohan, an admitted co-sharer of the suit property being alive and not having been made a party to the suit it was bad for defect of party. On such findings the learned Subordinate judge dismissed the suit by judgment dated 26.5.75.
